_comment: Stage-2 canonicalization corpus. Each item carries: a sample `input` (a raw document, kept for reference + future Stage-1 LLM judging), the `proposal` schema that Stage 1 would emit for it, and an `expected_concept` label the scorer groups by. Items sharing a concept SHOULD collapse to one canonical; if they don't, that's dup explosion. NOTE: the service requires `field_descriptions` for every field (used for semantic matching). To grow this to thousands, append items (or generate proposals via the node ingestion LLM and cache them here). An item may ALSO carry `expected_decompose: [conceptA, conceptB, ...]` (>= 2 concepts) when its record SHOULD split across multiple PRE-EXISTING canonicals — e.g. an Order that carries a Customer + a shipping Address + Line Items, each of which is already a registered canonical. Such an item ought to register as a COMPOSED schema that references those component canonicals via SchemaRefs instead of re-inlining a mega-schema; the `composed`/`reuse_rate` metrics measure how close the service gets. Order matters: list each component concept's own item BEFORE the composite so the components exist when the composite is replayed. A composite's `ref_fields` map each nested field to the component canonical it should reuse (e.g. `ship_to -> "Postal Address"`) and its `field_descriptions` entry carries that canonical's purpose so the per-component purpose gate (τ_purpose 0.88) fires. The harness scores COMPOSED off the service's authoritative wire marker (`AddSchemaResponse.composed`, set only on the apply path's `SchemaAddOutcome::Composed`), NOT off the mere presence of `ref_fields` — so with the apply path OFF (`--no-compositional`) the same proposal registers as NEW (composed 0/2), the before-state the metric quantifies, vs composed 2/2 with the apply path on.
